- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 1–2%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10-day average of true prices is > 10% above recent 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if last 3 days of true prices show upward trend, model often misses it — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” (e.g., +0.6 → -0.6 → +0.6), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to match sentiment reversal pattern 1–2 days ahead.
